lab.mission: LiGHT develops optical imaging and metrology systems that see beneath surfaces without cutting, staining or ionising radiation. We build multimodal, multiscale instruments around optical coherence tomography, hyperspectral imaging and optical microscopy, and take them from the optical bench to the clinic, the field and the factory floor: for earlier, non-invasive diagnosis of oral and other diseases, and for non-destructive inspection in industry and agriculture.

bio.short: Naresh Kumar Ravichandran is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Engineering Design at IIT Madras, where he leads the LiGHT lab (Light in Guided-wave Healthcare & Testing). His research develops multimodal, multiscale optical imaging and metrology systems based on optical coherence tomography, hyperspectral imaging and optical microscopy for biomedical diagnostics and industrial non-destructive inspection.
long: Naresh Kumar Ravichandran is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Engineering Design at the Indian Institute of Technology Madras (since March 2025), where he leads the LiGHT lab — Light in Guided-wave Healthcare & Testing. He received the IIT Madras Young Faculty Fellowship on joining.

Before IIT Madras he spent five years (2020–2025) as a Senior Postdoctoral Researcher with Dr. Kye-Sung Lee at the Korea Basic Science Institute (KBSI), Daejeon, where he designed and built multimodal, multiscale microscopes that combine optical coherence microscopy with line-confocal fluorescence and multiphoton microscopy, including label-free photothermal OCM for locating regions of interest in volumetric specimens, long-term live-cell monitoring of 3D bio-chips, and micro-elastography of human tendon.

He received his M.S. (2016, advisor Prof. Jeehyun Kim) and Ph.D. (2020, advisor Prof. Mansik Jeon) in Electronics Engineering from Kyungpook National University, Daegu, South Korea, where his doctoral work on optical coherence tomography for dental, biological and agricultural specimens received the Best Ph.D. Thesis award of the Graduate School of Electronics Engineering. He received his B.E. in Electronics & Communication Engineering from St. Peter's University, Tamil Nadu, in 2012.

He has co-authored more than 50 peer-reviewed publications and holds a Korean patent on structured-illumination microscopy. He serves as a guest editor for MDPI Diagnostics and Photonics and as a reviewer for Optica, Elsevier and MDPI journals.

research_themes.title: Multimodal 3D Live-Cell & Tissue Imaging
research_themes.summary: A multimode, multiscale microscope that co-registers optical coherence microscopy (OCM) with line-confocal fluorescence microscopy (LC-FM) and multiphoton microscopy. Label-free OCM maps the whole volume and steers high-magnification fluorescence only where it is needed, so living 3D cultures can be followed for days with less photobleaching and phototoxicity.

results.text: Co-registered OCM and LC-FM with interchangeable objectives (10× to 60×), so label-free OCM volumes guide high-resolution 3D fluorescence directly at the chosen region.
Rapidly located protrusions of tumour spheroids and narrow tubular branches of self-assembled vascular networks on a biochip, then imaged them instantly at high resolution.
Monitored tumour spheroids mixed with extracellular matrix over five days, revealing proliferation and migration relative to the ECM without spending fluorescence on navigation.
Developed a long-term storable gel-laden chip composite for high-throughput 3D liver models.

figures.caption: OCM and fluorescence overlays of a tumour spheroid on day 1 and day 5, with OCM-based 3D guidance
figures.credit: Ravichandran et al., Opt. Laser Technol. 179, 111351 (2024), CC BY 4.0

figures.caption: OCM-navigated imaging of a self-assembled 3D vascular network
figures.credit: Ravichandran et al., Opt. Laser Technol. 179, 111351 (2024), CC BY 4.0

figures.caption: Workflow: ROI selection in 10× OCM, aiming with 60× OCM, then high-resolution 3D fluorescence
figures.credit: Ravichandran et al., Opt. Laser Technol. 179, 111351 (2024), CC BY 4.0

figures.caption: Multimode OCM–LC-FM system with an environment-controlled live-cell chamber
figures.credit: Ravichandran et al., Opt. Laser Technol. 179, 111351 (2024), CC BY 4.0

research_themes.title: Line-Scan Confocal Fluorescence Microscopy
research_themes.tagline: Fast optical sectioning for thick specimens
research_themes.summary: Epi-illumination line-scan confocal microscopy with rolling-shutter detection for fast volumetric fluorescence imaging, together with simple strategies that sharpen optical sectioning in thick, scattering samples such as organoids and cleared tissue.

results.text: Temporally modulated scanning illumination (TMSI): a sinusoidal intensity modulation with a period of twice the line-beam width, synchronised to the rolling shutter, suppresses out-of-focus fluorescence with no hardware modification.
Showed enhanced sectioning and contrast on 15 µm fluorescent beads, a ~30 µm corn-grain section and a ~180 µm optically cleared mouse kidney, while keeping real-time imaging rates.
Built line-confocal FM into the multimodal OCM platform for 60× fluorescence at OCM-selected regions of live 3D cultures.

figures.caption: Cleared mouse kidney: line-scan confocal without (left) and with TMSI (right)
figures.credit: Lee, …, Ravichandran, Appl. Phys. Lett. 128, 013701 (2026); reproduced with permission of AIP Publishing

figures.caption: Fluorescent beads and corn-grain cells: widefield, line-scan confocal and TMSI
figures.credit: Lee, …, Ravichandran, Appl. Phys. Lett. 128, 013701 (2026); reproduced with permission of AIP Publishing

figures.caption: 60× LC-FM navigated by OCM for live-cell monitoring over days 1–5
figures.credit: Ravichandran et al., Opt. Laser Technol. 179, 111351 (2024), CC BY 4.0

research_themes.title: Multiphoton Microscopy: SHG · THG · 2PEF · 3PEF
research_themes.tagline: Label-free nonlinear contrast, guided by photothermal OCM
research_themes.summary: Multiphoton microscopes for second- and third-harmonic generation (SHG, THG) and two- and three-photon excited fluorescence (2PEF, 3PEF), including simultaneous epi- and trans-detection. Label-free photothermal OCM finds the region of interest first, so the femtosecond laser is used only where high-resolution nonlinear imaging is needed.

results.text: Phase-differentiated photothermal OCM detects the weak photothermal response that the MPM laser, at reduced power, induces in endogenous absorbers, locating the multiphoton focus on the region of interest.
With automated x–y movement, navigated the MPM focal plane through volumetric samples of 4 mm × 4 mm × 1 mm for targeted SHG imaging of phantoms and a biological specimen.
Built multiphoton systems for SHG/THG and 2PEF/3PEF with simultaneous epi- and trans-detection, and MPM–OCM micro-elastography of human tendon (KBSI projects).

figures.caption: Collagen network imaged by OCM (zoomed) and by multiphoton microscopy
figures.credit: Ravichandran et al., Sci. Rep. 13, 3625 (2023), CC BY 4.0

figures.caption: Photothermal-OCM-guided SHG images and the photothermal signal used to find the focus
figures.credit: Ravichandran et al., Sci. Rep. 13, 3625 (2023), CC BY 4.0

figures.caption: Multimodal platform: photothermal OCM combined with a multiphoton microscope
figures.credit: Ravichandran et al., Sci. Rep. 13, 3625 (2023), CC BY 4.0

research_themes.title: Optical Coherence Tomography & Microscopy
research_themes.summary: Spectral-domain and swept-source OCT, optical coherence microscopy, and handheld, wearable and compact OCT. Our work spans system design, dispersion and path-length compensation, Doppler and speckle-variance contrast, and fast 3D visualisation.

results.text: Bi-directional SD-OCT that extends imaging depth using a single spectrometer.
Integrated spectrally encoded confocal microscopy and OCT with automatic co-registration, OCT-guided depth targeting and speckle reduction, at about 7 frames/s with GPU processing.
Handheld Doppler OCT for blood-flow imaging, and an ultra-compact OCT built on a Raspberry Pi single-board computer.

figures.caption: Bi-directional SD-OCT for depth-enhanced imaging
figures.credit: Ravichandran et al., J. Biomed. Opt. 21(7), 076005 (2016)

figures.caption: Bench-top OCT system built during the M.S./Ph.D. at KNU
figures.credit: From the career roadmap

research_themes.title: Multimodal Optical Entomology
research_themes.summary: Non-destructive optical imaging of mosquitoes, ticks and other insects that carry disease. OCT shows internal organs in 3D without dissection, staining or ionising radiation, and multiphoton microscopy adds label-free nonlinear (SHG) contrast at targeted regions. Together they support comparative anatomy and studies of vector biology.

results.text: 3D OCT of Anopheles sinensis anatomy: head, thorax, abdomen and the foregut, midgut and hindgut, validated against histology.

Bidirectional swept-source OCT with a rotating sample arm merged top and bottom volumes to image whole mosquitoes. It compared Anopheles, Aedes and Culex species and segmented the heart, midgut, dorsal and ventral crops and abdominal ganglia.
SD-OCT (6.2 µm axial, 2.46 µm lateral resolution) identified salivary glands, midgut, genital orifice and ovary in hard ticks without dissection.
Photothermal-OCM-guided multiphoton (SHG) imaging was demonstrated on a fixed insect specimen.

figures.caption: OCT for entomology: internal anatomy of mosquito pupa, larva and adult
figures.credit: Ravichandran et al., Sensors 17, 1897 (2017), CC BY

figures.caption: Photothermal-OCM-guided SHG imaging, demonstrated on a fixed insect specimen
figures.credit: Ravichandran et al., Sci. Rep. 13, 3625 (2023), CC BY 4.0

research_themes.title: Oral & Dental Optical Diagnostics
research_themes.summary: Quantitative OCT of teeth, gingiva and alveolar bone for orthodontics and dentistry. LiGHT now extends this to multimodal optical imaging, including hyperspectral imaging, for earlier, non-invasive detection of oral cancer and other oral pathologies.

results.text: 3D OCT tracked enamel microcrack progression after metal and ceramic bracket debonding in 16 premolars, with significant changes in crack length, width and number.
An intensity-based layer-segmentation algorithm measured micron-scale enamel loss after each step of bracket bonding and debonding.
2D and 3D OCT revealed microcracks and micro-elevations in cortical bone around 80 orthodontic micro-implants inserted by different methods and at different angles.
An averaged-intensity-difference algorithm automatically identified the human gingival sulcus in OCT images.

figures.caption: OCT assessment of cortical-bone microdamage around orthodontic micro-implants
figures.credit: Lakshmikantha, Ravichandran et al., Sci. Rep. 9, 3242 (2019), CC BY

figures.caption: Measuring enamel loss after etching and prophylaxis with OCT
figures.credit: Ravichandran et al., J. Healthc. Eng. 2019, 8973825, CC BY

figures.caption: Automated gingival sulcus measurement in OCT images
figures.credit: Ravichandran et al., IEEE Access 7, 73076 (2019), CC BY

research_themes.title: Non-Destructive Industrial & Agricultural Inspection
research_themes.tagline: Optical metrology for Industry 4.0 and the field
research_themes.summary: OCT-based inspection of multilayer industrial parts, together with portable OCT for crops, seeds and plant disease in the field.

results.text: Review of OCT for Industry 4.0 covering inspection of displays, thin films, microelectronics, PCBs, laser-based manufacturing and coatings, with open challenges and AI-enabled directions.
Preprint: a 400 kHz swept-source OCT at 1300 nm reconstructed a subsurface defect 0.323 mm below the surface of a SiC focus ring, with a relative volumetric error below 0.01 %.
Released an open OCT dataset for pre-identifying apple and persimmon leaf disease from palisade and spongy-layer thickness.
Wearable backpack OCT for in-field leaf inspection, and in vivo monitoring of seed growth under salt stress.

figures.caption: Non-destructive OCT monitoring of Capsicum annuum seed growth under NaCl stress
figures.credit: Ravichandran et al., Sensors 17, 2887 (2017), CC BY

figures.caption: Wearable backpack OCT for in-field leaf inspection
figures.credit: Wijesinghe, …, Ravichandran et al., Appl. Opt. 56(9), D108 (2017)

figures.caption: OCT quantification of moisture in mushroom tissue layers during storage
figures.credit: Ravichandran et al., IJAER 12(15), 5011 (2017)

research_themes.title: Computational Imaging & AI-Assisted Analysis
research_themes.tagline: From optical volumes to quantitative decisions
research_themes.summary: Signal processing, segmentation and deep-learning pipelines that turn OCT and microscopy data into measurements and classifications.

results.text: Combined YOLOv8 with OCT to identify okra flower buds and quantify emasculation depth through the sepal and petal layers, outperforming colour-histogram and imaging baselines.
Classified seed cultivars by OCT intensity and depth-profile analysis.
Fully automated, real-time segmentation of retinal layers in OCT images.

figures.caption: Automated OCT-based seed classification pipeline
figures.credit: Manattayil, Ravichandran et al., Sensors 18, 2500 (2018), CC BY
